chunks: And ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said:
Whatever the mudarib spends during his travel is from the joint capital; then when he arrives at his town, whatever he spends is from his own share.

key_terms.اَلْمُضَارِبُ: the investment agent or working partner in a mudarabah agreement
key_terms.بَلْدَتَهُ: his home town or place of residence
key_terms.جَمْعِ الْمَالِ: the pooled or joint capital of the partnership
key_terms.سَفَرِهِ: his journey undertaken for the business
key_terms.نَصِيبِهِ: his own portion or personal share

ai.seo_question: In mudarabah, are the agent's travel expenses taken from the business capital or from his own share?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning mudarabah: the working partner's expenses during business travel are charged to the shared capital. Once he returns home, his personal expenditures are no longer treated as business expenses and come from his own share.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3846 - Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:
"Whatever the partner spends during his travel is taken from the joint capital. However, when he returns to his town, whatever he spends is from his own share."
